scenes.subtitle: Consent broker cho AI agent
scenes.narration: An AI agent wants your whole document folder. TrustGate gives it only what you approve - for one purpose, for a set time, and revocable at any moment.
Your documents are encrypted in the browser with AES-256-GCM. The server only ever stores ciphertext.
A playbook defines what may be shared, and for whom. The agent proposes the minimum set of documents.
Now you decide. Unlock the vault, uncheck the optional document, choose a fifteen-minute lifetime. The server enforces the scope.
The agent receives only what you approved, sealed to a key that expires with the grant. Every step is logged.
The agent has no console of its own. It is an API client, and everything it does is logged.
As an administrator, dump the entire database. Every document is ciphertext. No plaintext, no keys, and your passphrase never reaches the server.
Try to grant yourself administrator. The system does not refuse - it downgrades you into a pending change request: zero of two approvals. Your role has not changed.
And the agent cannot ask for anything outside its scope. Medical records are refused: four-oh-three, out of scope, and it is logged.
Direct changes are blocked: four-oh-nine, quorum required. The legitimate path is a change request - admin one re-authenticates and signs.
Admin two signs as well. Two signatures reach the quorum threshold - and only then does the change execute.
Consent is revocable mid-flight. Watch a slow agent run step through the grant.
Revoke the grant. The key is deleted - crypto-shredding - and the agent fails at its very next step: failed, revoked.
Every access is written to an append-only hash chain. Verify the chain, and the system proves nothing was altered.

scenes.subtitle: Laravel · React · WebCrypto · AES-256-GCM · Hash-chained audit
scenes.narration: TrustGate: a vault and consent broker for AI agents. Laravel, React, WebCrypto, AES-256-GCM, hash-chained audit. A prototype - encryption is browser-side fallback mode, not yet trustless.
